ideas: Where you were and who you were with

phrases.meaning: confusion in a very different culture

phrases.phrase: see things from a different perspective

model: I'd like to talk about a cultural difference that surprised me when I started working with a Dutch company two years ago. I was part of a small project team, and we had weekly video meetings with colleagues in Amsterdam. In my first meeting, I presented a plan that I'd worked on for days, and one of the Dutch managers simply said, 'I don't think this will work,' and explained why. That really caught me off guard. In Vietnam, criticism is usually given very gently, and people often beat around the bush to avoid embarrassing anyone. Being so direct, especially with a new colleague, would probably be considered rude here. Honestly, I felt a bit hurt that evening. But later, a colleague told me that in the Netherlands, directness is seen as a sign of honesty and respect. They get straight to the point because they don't want to waste anyone's time. Although it wasn't easy at first, I gradually learned not to take it personally. Whereas I used to spend ages trying to guess what people really meant, now I actually appreciate knowing exactly where I stand. It wasn't a huge culture shock, but it definitely made me see things from a different perspective. I think it's made me more open-minded, and I've even become a little more direct myself, although I'm still more polite than my Dutch colleagues.
